requirement:
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.refactor_skill.workflow` states what the `habeas-refactor` skill must direct agents to do. It prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface. The clauses describe the content of the skill document, so I treated them as observable behavior. The one root is `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md`, and I checked each clause against its `Workflow` section, `section[Habeas%20refactor]/section[Workflow]`.

- **Own edits, kept separate from changes to the moved code or text:** step 1 says to make the move with your own edits. It says to change nothing else, to keep the moved text exactly as it was, and to leave references and anchors for the command to rewrite.
- **Dry run with a mapping for every moved file, node and definition name:** step 2 runs `habeas refactor --dry-run` with one `--map` for each moved file or directory, node, and definition name. It gives an example of each form.
- **Review the report, including unchanged records and rationale spans:** step 3 covers "Would rewrite", "Would change" with the rationale code spans that still mention an old path, and "Would leave ... unchanged". It also says to show the spans to the user.
- **Run without `--dry-run`:** step 4.
- **Confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records are stale:** step 5.
- **Commit before changing behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the habeas-evidence skill:** step 6 commits the move, rewritten references and `evidence/` changes before any behavior or text change. Step 7 reassesses with `habeas author --all`, following the habeas-evidence skill.

The skill covers every clause, and no structural obligation needs further implementation evidence.

behavioral: The only test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_refactor_skill_moves_first_then_updates_evidence_with_habeas_refactor]`. It calls `assert_in_order`, which runs `assert_text_in_order` over `bundled_skill("habeas-refactor")`. The helper panics unless each phrase appears after the previous one in the whitespace-collapsed skill text. The subject's obligations all concern what the skill directs agents to do, so phrase assertions on the skill text are a direct check of them.

Obligations and the assertions that cover them:
- **Agents make the move with their own edits, kept separate from changes to the moved code or text.** The test asserts "Make the move with your own edits" and "Change nothing else in this step".
- **Run `habeas refactor --dry-run` with a mapping for every moved file, node and definition name.** The test asserts the full phrase "`habeas refactor --dry-run` with one `--map <old>=<new>` for every moved file or directory, node, and definition name". The cited `requirements.refactor.dry_run` and `requirements.refactor.mappings` are context only, so I did not reassess their tests.
- **Review the report, including records left unchanged and the rationale spans it lists.** The test asserts "Review the report". It also asserts "lists the records it updates, with each code span in their rationales that still mentions an old path", which is the `requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched` span listing. It also asserts "lists records a mapping affects that fail a check", which is the records left unchanged.
- **Run without `--dry-run`.** The test asserts "Run the same command without `--dry-run`".
- **Confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records are stale.** The test asserts "`habeas status`. Only the records the report left unchanged".
- **Commit the move and evidence update before changing behavior.** The test asserts "Commit the move, the rewritten references, and the `evidence/` changes together, before any change to behavior or text".
- **Then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the habeas-evidence skill.** The test asserts "Next, reassess what remains stale with `habeas author --all`, following the habeas-evidence skill".

Because the phrases must appear in order, the test also enforces the required sequence: move, dry run, review, real run, status, commit, then reassess. I read the Workflow step 1 text in `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md`, which matches the asserted phrases. If the skill dropped, reworded or reordered any of these steps, the test would fail. I found no obligation without an assertion and no plausible violating skill text that the test would accept.

text: :::{req} refactor_skill.workflow
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
:::{req} dry_run
With `--dry-run`, `habeas refactor` MUST report every change it would make,
in the same form as {cite}`requirements.refactor.command`, and MUST write
nothing.
:::{req} mappings
Each `--map` MUST have one of these forms:
- a file or directory path, which maps that file, or every file under that
directory, to the same relative path under the new side;
- `<file>#<selector>`, which maps one outline node, and its outline
descendants, to the node at the new file and selector;
- a definition name, which maps that full name, and every full name beginning
with it followed by `.`, to the same suffix under the new name.
A mapping whose old side names a recorded definition, or a prefix of one
followed by `.`, MUST be a definition-name mapping.
:::{req} rationale.untouched
`habeas refactor` MUST NOT change rationale text other than the spans
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.names`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.paths`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.addresses` cover. For each changed
record, it MUST list the other code spans in the rationale that contain an old
side of a path or node mapping, so the user can review them.
